sampling_model.design: Conditional on the revealed \(G\), draw the capped balanced reservoir capsule \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\); the only inferential randomness is its reservoir, arm-swap, and assignment randomization.
sampling_model.units: The finite population \(V\) and its potential-outcome schedule are fixed conditional on \(G\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary assignment forces all closed neighborhoods of \(T\) to treatment and all closed neighborhoods of \(C_0\) to control, with fair independent assignments elsewhere.
sampling_model.overlap: On an accepted capsule, every focal endpoint has positive inclusion probability of order \(k/n\), derived in Theorem 1 rather than assumed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no super-population nuisances; exact inclusion and Rao--Blackwell weights are finite design functionals, with polynomial-time approximation posed separately in Open-ended Question 1.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For random \(d\)-regular \(G\) with \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\) with probability \(1-o(1)\).
The modified Horvitz--Thompson estimator under the Conflict Graph Design has variance at most \(12.5\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) times the two endpoint empirical second moments.
The neighborhood-union construction gives a one-sided treated-component upper bound under controlled codegrees and leaves the full estimator open.
A greedy independent focal set has size at least \(n\log s/s\) with high probability in the paper's Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi regime.
Theorem 4 and Corollary 5 of arXiv:2210.08698v3 compare uniform root mean-squared error of the design-based Riesz estimator with the scaled norm of its variance operator.
The largest balanced independent sets in generic random bipartite graphs have density \((2+o_d(1))\log d/d\), with a factor-two local-algorithm barrier.

body.tldr: A one-shot full-GATE experiment on a revealed random \(d\)-regular network is recast as balanced sampling in its bipartite two-copy exposure conflict graph. A fixed-cardinality reservoir capsule selects \(k\asymp n\log d/d^2\) compatible treated and control focal units, uses an arm swap to remove the global complement-mixture mode, and Rao--Blackwellizes the focal Horvitz--Thompson estimator into the published observed-data regime. The central theorem bounds the signed normalized exposure-covariance operator by \(O(d^2/\log d)\); together with an all-procedure Bayes lower bound, this yields \(R_2(G)\asymp d^2/[n\log d]\) with high probability.

project_justification.gap: The published unrestricted minimax theory leaves \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\) for random regular full GATE, while the sharper neighborhood-union construction is one-sided and the archived seed-union route fails at a centered Boolean radius-two operator bound.
project_justification.niche: The two-copy GATE conflict graph is bipartite, so a balanced stable set can protect both endpoint denominators without using an experiment-wide design/complement mixture. Fixed focal cardinalities also expose a covariance kernel whose dangerous common arm mode is absent by construction.
project_justification.fill: The project constructs a samplable balanced reservoir capsule, proves its exact observed-data risk certificate, derives a diagonal-scale two-arm covariance-operator bound on typical random regular graphs, and matches it with a lower bound against all procedures.

body.related_work: Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje define the identical endpoint-\(L^2\) minimax experiment under the standard random-regular condition \(d=o(\sqrt n)\) and leave its full-GATE rate between \(d/n\) and \(d^2/n\); the focused condition \(d\to\infty\) used here is not theirs. Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw provide the covariance-operator template and an \(O(\lambda(H_G)/n)\) conflict-priority guarantee, which is \(O(d^2/n)\) here. Li and Li motivate denominator protection through neighborhood unions and explicitly stop at a one-sided estimator, making two-arm cross-covariance the first changed proof step. Theorem 4 and Corollary 5 of Harshaw, S\"avje, and Wang, arXiv:2210.08698v3 of 14 August 2025, supply the verified Riesz variance-operator comparison used to turn normalized exposure covariance into uniform design-based risk. Cai, Zhang, and Airoldi show how independent focal sets create logarithmic effective-sample gains under a different target and stronger response model. Perkins and Wang identify the same logarithmic balanced-stable-set scale in generic random bipartite graphs but do not address the structured GATE graph or estimator covariance. Karrer and coauthors provide the concrete large-scale global-rollout consumer for a degree-explicit precision frontier.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The load-bearing unproved step is Theorem 1's operator bound, not stable-set size alone. The proof must control the accepted-reservoir conditioning, heterogeneous conditional inclusion probabilities, and all treated--control covariance blocks uniformly for \(d=o(\sqrt n)\). Bounding entries or the maximum codegree separately is insufficient. The embedded presolve route is to expand exact hypergeometric avoidance probabilities before taking norms, isolate the fixed-cardinality negative modes, and use a Schur-complement bound for the remaining overlap kernel. The archived Boolean-power estimate is retained only as a diagnostic and is not assumed.
body.honest_scope: Propositions 1--2 and Lemma 1 are finite design identities to be verified. The new open mathematical content is the random-regular covariance theorem and the all-procedure lower audit that together imply the matched frontier. Exact enumeration makes the procedure evaluable but can be exponential; Open-ended Question 1 asks whether the structured graph permits a polynomial-time estimator and observable certificate. The proposal does not claim a studentized CLT, bounded outcomes, additive interference, or that any deployed social network is uniformly random regular.
